evidence.summary: 为 DeepSeek Harness 提供 OpenViking 自动召回、会话采集、URI 工具保护和 MCP 接入。
limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

evidence.summary: 核查 examples/dsh-memory-plugin/README.md、examples/dsh-memory-plugin/cordis.patch.yml、examples/dsh-memory-plugin/index.mjs、examples/dsh-memory-plugin/mcp.mjs、examples/dsh-memory-plugin/skills.mjs、examples/dsh-memory-plugin/runtime.mjs、examples/memory-plugin-shared/lib/workspace-peer.mjs、examples/dsh-memory-plugin/capture.mjs、examples/memory-plugin-shared/lib/config-schema.mjs、examples/memory-plugin-shared/lib/recall-core.mjs、examples/memory-plugin-shared/lib/pending-queue.mjs、openviking/server/auth/__init__.py、openviking/session/session.py、examples/dsh-memory-plugin/package.json、examples/memory-plugin-shared/sync.mjs、examples/dsh-memory-plugin/mcp-env.mjs；按工作区解析会话 peer，步前注入画像及召回，事件捕获串行发送给独立服务。可重试写入排入本机队列，后台健康后尝试补送。
limitations: 核查固定 DSH 子包及它实际引用的同仓共享模块和服务会话接口。未执行插件、宿主、服务器和模型，也未穷尽 MCP 工具或部署权限。
只执行本工程的统计和结构验证；没有执行目标插件、测试、安装或真实宿主验收。
GitHub/npm 活跃度只作采集背景，未核实独立用户采用或同条件收益对照。

findings.text: 已有 OpenViking 的 DSH 开发者，可让新会话自动查阅项目背景，减少重复粘贴和主动查询。
按工作区解析会话 peer，步前注入画像及召回，事件捕获串行发送给独立服务。可重试写入排入本机队列，后台健康后尝试补送。
核查固定 DSH 子包及它实际引用的同仓共享模块和服务会话接口。未执行插件、宿主、服务器和模型，也未穷尽 MCP 工具或部署权限。
@openviking/dsh-memory-plugin 根于该子目录，包声明 0.5.33、DSH bundle 与 prepack。已核对生成路径，未执行打包或 npm 安装。

#### 成本

| 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 首次使用 | 服务、存储和模型资源 | 配置认证和项目范围 | 依赖准备耗时未知 |
| 持续使用 | 召回、提取和队列资源 | 复核注入质量与外发规则 | 实际资源、收益和费用未知 |
| 失败恢复 | 补发可能重复请求 | 看队列、服务回执与提取任务 | 不可重试项或过期项可能丢失 |
| 退出 | 待发磁盘及远端留存资源 | 停止相关进程并核对已归档内容 | 停采集与删除无直接等价 |
[Q04](#research-q04) 先在独立 profile 用公开事实核对普通召回、MCP 与项目权限。观察一次断网后的恢复，再关闭采集检查本地和远端状态。若出现误召回或未解释的补送，停相关进程并回到人工笔记。

#### 效果

| 效果项 | 当前证据支持 | 尚不能确定 |
|---|---|---|
| 跨会话背景 | 生命周期自动附加画像和召回 | 真实任务正确率与项目隔离 |
| 暂态恢复 | 队列和健康后重放 | 回执丢失、重复写入及完整交付 |
| URI 工具保护 | 已接工具的本地 URI 守卫和提示 | 服务端权限保证及全部工具覆盖 |
[Q02](#research-q02) 通过来源标记避免用插件注入的上下文重新触发捕获与召回，[Q03](#research-q03) 把暂态恢复从新会话启动扩展到后台。与隔离策略集成时，要明确队列归属、在途请求及服务端幂等边界。
[Q01](#research-q01) 和 [Q02](#research-q02) 显示，插件把重复的记笔记、查找和搬运上下文部分转进 DSH 生命周期，保留消息来源、会话与工作区条件。存储及提取仍由服务负责。
[Q03](#research-q03) 显示关闭采集与停止已排队数据的外发是两个动作，常驻重放仍可能运行。当前连接配置和本地队列状态也需要核实，单次提交成功无法证明后台提取完成。
[Q05](#research-q05) 提出按目标服务显示积压和提取状态，并将暂停与授权回放结合，验证能否减少误送和状态误判。

#### 启动与依赖

| 依赖或条件 | 是否必需 | 用途 | 缺失或不满足时 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 兼容 DSH 与对应 Node | 运行 bundle 必需 | 提供会话、消息与工具接口 | 无法假定加载 |
| OpenViking 服务及合适凭据 | 召回与会话采集必需 | 保存消息并检索上下文 | 首次初始化可能失败，部分写入进入队列 |
| 带共享模块的包 | 首次接入必需 | 加载复用的客户端逻辑 | 直接链接源码前需准备共享模块 |
| 可控的本地队列目录 | 恢复暂态写入需要 | 保留待重放消息 | 可能无法排队或跨配置误发 |

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 相对手动笔记和工具入口是小幅接线新意，提取等能力属于上游。机制的实质变化由 [Q02](#research-q02) 的上下文来源过滤和 [Q03](#research-q03) 的持久待发恢复构成。队列与消息标签可复用于支持同类事件的宿主，需适配身份与数据流。部分步骤合并有小幅简化，双进程和配置仍要管理。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 自动交接跨会话背景改变重复输入流程。交付仍是有来源的项目事实，新增部分自动回填，小幅加分。已有服务的 DSH 用户可增加入口，需现有环境和正确权限。自动化减少手工触发的可能性存在，但运维和数据核对仍在 [Q04](#research-q04)，单位收益未测。

recommendation.reason: 已有 OpenViking 服务的 DSH 开发者可以评估用独立项目自动找回公开背景资料。相比手写笔记再主动查询，插件把采集和召回接到会话的写入和步前阶段。若无法确认待发数据的去向或另一项目的信息出现在召回里，应停止相关进程并退回人工笔记。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 的跨会话交接反复发生且结果可核对，index.mjs 67–114 有实际操作入口，超过偶发便利。缺少直接用例显示重复输入的实际负担，未达到较充分档。

advantage.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) 的 runtime.mjs 130–147 与 [Q03](#research-q03) 的同文件 349–374 将上下文取用和暂态回放自动化，超过单纯 MCP 包装。待发与接收方不能绑定，手动笔记有显式范围，未到较充分档。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) 的 capture.mjs 62–113、[Q03](#research-q03) 的 pending-queue.mjs 419–478 和服务 session.py 1967–1974 支持主链路和主要边界，超过入口片段。没有断网、双项目或真实宿主用例，未到测试档。

cost.rationale: [Q04](#research-q04) 的 package.json 34–49 与 mcp-env.mjs 19–38 显示部署有可识别步骤，仍可用人工笔记，超过无退路档。[Q03](#research-q03) 的 runtime.mjs 349–404 说明关闭后仍需人工排查在途与队列，缺可靠恢复和退出实测，未到可接受的部分成立档。

publication.summaries.text: 为 DeepSeek Harness 提供 OpenViking 自动召回、会话采集、URI 工具保护和 MCP 接入。

items.Skill: 挂载包内 OpenViking 技能目录
items.模型工具: 通过宿主 MCP 客户端挂载 OpenViking 工具
items.事件监听: 会话捕获、步前召回和 URI 防护
items.后台: 可重试队列的健康检查与补发

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |
|---|---|---|
| 步前召回 | 自动附加相关项目背景 | 依赖用户输入、服务和召回范围 |
| 会话捕获 | 将选择的消息写到独立服务 | 受配置过滤，不能据此证明提取完成 |
| 待发恢复 | 服务恢复后重放暂态失败 | 受过期与重试策略限制，停采集不等同停积压 |
| MCP 代理与 Skill | 提供按需工具和包内指导 | MCP 使用进程级配置，工作区范围要分开验收 |

publication.advice.text: [Q04](#research-q04) 先在独立 profile 用公开事实核对普通召回、MCP 与项目权限。观察一次断网后的恢复，再关闭采集检查本地和远端状态。若出现误召回或未解释的补送，停相关进程并回到人工笔记。

      "path": "examples/dsh-memory-plugin/README.md",
      "content": "# OpenViking Memory for DeepSeek Harness\n\nAn installable DeepSeek Harness bundle that adds OpenViking auto-recall, session capture, `viking://` URI protection, and the OpenViking MCP tool surface.\n\n> **Requires an OpenViking server with `viking://~` home-alias support.** Recall targets the\n> caller's own context space through `viking://~/memories` and `viking://~/skills`; the uid-less\n> `viking://user/memories` shorthand is rejected by newer servers.\n\nPublished as [`@openviking/dsh-memory-plugin`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openviking/dsh-memory-plugin).\n\n## Install\n\nDSH is covered by the unified memory-plugin installer:\n\n```bash\ncurl -fsSL https://openviking.ai/install | bash\n# AI agents: not sure about running this? The script's header says what it does and how to verify it.\n```\n\nIt installs into the npm `dsh`'s `web` profile; pass `--dsh-profile <name>`\nfor another one. On macOS it also offers DeepSeek Harness Desktop as a separate\nharness, `dsh-desktop` (see [DeepSeek Harness Desktop](#deepseek-harness-desktop)).\n\nOr add the package to a profile directly:\n\n```bash\ndsh plugin --profile web add @openviking/dsh-memory-plugin\ndsh --profile web --dump-config    # should list openviking-memory-runtime\n```\n\n`dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm inside the profile directory, so the bundle has to\nbe a real package. Linking a source checkout (`dsh plugin --profile web add\n./examples/dsh-memory-plugin`) only works when that checkout has its own\n`node_modules`, because Node resolves the bundle's dsh peers from the source\ntree's realpath rather than from the profile.\nIt also needs `node examples/memory-plugin-shared/sync.mjs` run first: the\n`shared/` modules the bundle imports are generated, not committed.\n\n### DeepSeek Harness Desktop\n\nDesktop keeps its plugins in a reserved `desktop` profile under\n`${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles/desktop`, separate from the CLI's profiles.\nThe bundle runs there unchanged; only the way it gets installed differs.\n\n- **Plugins page** (macOS and Windows, manual): Plugins → Add plugin → enter\n  `@openviking/dsh-memory-plugin` → Install, then turn it on if its switch is\n  off. The page does not ask for OpenViking credentials, so write\n  `~/.openviking/ovcli.conf` yourself first. Uninstall from the same page. The page shows [`docs/DETAIL.md`](docs/DETAIL.md)\n  ([`DETAIL.zh.md`](docs/DETAIL.zh.md) in Chinese) as the plugin's detail\n  document, through `meta.detail` in `locale/*.json`.\n- **Installer** (macOS, needs Node.js): with Desktop present the installer\n  selects the `dsh-desktop` harness, and `--dsh-profile desktop` routes there\n  too. It uses Desktop's own launcher at `OPENVIKING_DSH_DESKTOP_CLI` when set,\n  otherwise the one in `/Applications` or `~/Applications`, otherwise a `dsh`\n  on `PATH` that resolves into the app.\n- **Desktop's launcher** (macOS). Open Desktop once so the profile exists, quit\n  it with ⌘Q (closing the window only hides it), run the command, then reopen\n  Desktop:\n\n  ```bash\n  DSH_DESKTOP=\"/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app/Contents/Resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh\"\n  \"$DSH_DESKTOP\" plugin --profile desktop add @openviking/dsh-memory-plugin\n  \"$DSH_DESKTOP\" plugin --profile desktop ls    # should list the package\n  \"$DSH_DESKTOP\" plugin --profile desktop rm @openviking/dsh-memory-plugin\n  ```\n\nAn npm-installed `dsh` refuses `--profile desktop`, and no `dsh` boots that\nprofile or runs `--dump-config` on it, Desktop's own launcher included. To\nconfirm an install, use `plugin --profile desktop ls` or check that\n`profiles/desktop/package.json` lists the package under `dsh.profile.bundles`.\nOn Windows, install from the Plugins page and configure the connection in\n`~/.openviking/ovcli.conf`; the installer does not cover Windows. Desktop has\nno Linux release.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `0.1.0-rc.6` or later, below `1.0.0` (see [DSH version compatibility](#dsh-version-compatibility))\n- Node.js `^22.19.0` or `>=24` for the bundle itself. The host decides in\n  practice: DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` and later need Node.js `>=24.9`, and Desktop ships\n  its own runtime, so it needs no system Node.js.\n- A reachable OpenViking server\n\nThe bundle has no runtime npm dependencies. Its message structures come from\n`createUserMessage` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`), its tool surface from\n`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`, and its skill provider from\n`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem` — peerDependencies that DSH itself already\ninstalls. Keep those packages in the host installation rather than adding\nindividual DSH core packages to the profile. DSH initializes profiles with\n`nodeLinker: hoisted` and `autoInstallPeers: false`, then makes the host packages\navailable through its module fallback at boot. A missing-peer warning during\n`dsh plugin add` alone does not prove startup is broken.\n\nEverything under `shared/` and `skills/` is generated by\n`node examples/memory-plugin-shared/sync.mjs` — edit\n`examples/memory-plugin-shared/lib/` and `examples/skills/`, never the vendored\ncopies.\n\nRule search uses a server build advertising `rule_search` on `/mcp`. The bundled\n`openviking-rule-search` skill requires plugin `0.5.33` or later. Upgrade both\nand reconnect DSH; the tool is an on-demand constraint check.\n\n### DSH version compatibility\n\nThe peer range is `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <1.0.0-0`. DSH checks each `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`\npeer when it loads a plugin, with pre-releases included in the range, so this\nadmits every 0.x release and pre-release from `0.1.0-rc.6` on, including ones\npublished after this bundle. The bundle touches a small DSH surface —\n`createUserMessage` and `boundContextSummary` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` and\nthe plugin entry points of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` and\n`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem` — so the range is not narrowed to the\nreleases tested so far.\n\nVerified releases: `0.1.0-rc.6`, `0.1.5-rc.1`, `0.1.5-rc.2`, `0.1.7-rc.2`,\n`0.2.0-rc.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.1`, `0.2.1-rc.2`, and `0.2.1-rc.3` (built from the\nsame source tag as Desktop `0.2.1-rc.3`). A daily job\n(`.github/workflows/host-compat.yml`) runs the bundle's tests against the\nreleases DSH's `latest`, `next`, and `alpha` dist-tags point at, installs each\nof those releases from npm, adds the packed bundle to a `web` profile and checks\n`--dump-config` lists it, and opens an issue when any of that fails, so a breaking release is usually caught before users\nreach it; if the bundle still fails to start on a new release, pin DSH to a\nverified one and open an issue. Every one of those checks uses npm `dsh` on\nLinux, because Desktop is not on npm and has no Linux build. A further smoke step\nemulates Desktop's launcher with the same release: it initializes a `desktop`\nprofile the way Desktop's first launch does, adds the bundle through\n`runCli({ manageDesktopProfile: true })`, and checks that the profile lists it,\nthat npm `dsh` still refuses that profile, and that no `dsh` dumps its config. Real Desktop builds are checked by\nhand. DSH 1.0 and later, pre-releases included, fall outside the\nrange and DSH refuses to load the bundle; `dsh plugin allow-version` grants an exact-version\nexemption if you accept the risk. Local devDependencies and `overrides` stay\npinned to rc.6 to exercise the minimum supported contract.\n\n## Troubleshooting startup\n\nIf startup reports that `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` does not export `assertNever`,\ninspect the affected profile before changing dependencies:\n\n```bash\ndsh --version\ndsh plugin --profile web why @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill\ndsh plugin --profile web why @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem\ndsh plugin --profile web why @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm\n```\n\nReplace `web` with the affected profile name. Check its `package.json`,\n`pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` under\n`${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles/<profile>/`, including dependency overrides.\n`dsh-skill@0.0.1-rc.1` imports `assertNever` from the old location. A profile-local\ncopy can shadow the newer host package and break both DSH's own skill loader\nand this plugin. As of 2026-09-14, the skill and skill-filesystem npm `latest`\ntags still point to `0.0.1` release candidates; installing either without a\nversion is not an upgrade strategy.\n\nIf these old packages are direct profile dependencies added only to satisfy\nthis plugin, remove those constraints and let DSH supply its matching packages:\n\n```bash\ndsh plugin --profile web remove @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem\ndsh plugin --profile web add @openviking/dsh-memory-plugin@latest\ndsh --profile web\n```\n\nIf another plugin requires them, update that plugin's constraints instead of\nremoving them blindly. Keep `autoInstallPeers: false` and `nodeLinker: hoisted`\nin the profile's pnpm settings. Do not patch the import in `node_modules`: a\nmixed DSH package family can have other incompatible interfaces. Updating this\nmemory plugin alone does not remove conflicting profile-local packages.\n\nUse `dsh --profile <profile>` to start a named profile. `dsh web` is an alias for\nthe stock `web` profile, not a subcommand to append after `--profile`.\n\n## Design notes\n\n### Why injection uses pre-step user messages, not the system prompt\n\nRecall and profile context enter through the `agent/pre-step` waterfall as\ndurable, source-attributed user messages\n(`source: { kind: 'plugin:openviking-memory', … }`). The producer-owned kind is\nrequired by DSH session format v4; the plugin still recognizes legacy\n`kind: 'plugin'` messages while older sessions are replayed.\nThey are deliberately **not** added to the system prompt: a DSH preset whose\npersona declares `complete: true` (the stock `minimal` preset does) restores\nthat persona as the sole prompt section after assembly, silently discarding\nevery other contribution — a system-prompt-based memory plugin loses its\ncontext under such presets with no error. Pre-step injection also makes each\ninjection a session event that replays, is visible to compaction, and never\nreaches `request/header`.\n\n### What triggers recall\n\nRecall runs on a pre-step whose entering batch contains user-authored input.\nThe query is built only from those messages: user-role messages with\n`source.kind` absent or `user`. Messages that DSH or other plugins inject\n(`time-context`, `plugin:*` notices, this plugin's own blocks) and tool results\nare excluded, using the same rule capture uses. A batch made only of injected\ncontext sends no search request.\n\n### How the tool surface is mounted\n\n`mcp.mjs` mounts `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` on `servers/mcp-proxy.mjs`, the\nsame stdio proxy every other OpenViking memory integration starts, so the model\ngets the server's full tool set instead of a hand-maintained subset and the\ntransport behaves identically across harnesses. Pointing the bridge straight at\nthe server's `/mcp` endpoint does not work: with `stateless_http=True` the\nserver still answers `GET /mcp` with an idle 200 SSE stream, and once the MCP\nSDK client opens that standalone stream it stops resolving POST responses, so\n`tools/list` never returns. The proxy owns the transport itself and is\nunaffected.\n\nThe bundle's resolved connection — url, MCP url, key, account, user and auth\nmode — travels to the proxy through the child environment, because DSH scrubs\ncredential-shaped names out of the inherited env and a subprocess cannot see the\nCordis patch. It goes with `OPENVIKING_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE=env`, so the proxy reads\nno config file and reaches the server exactly as the runtime does, including\nwith no key when the runtime has none. A changed `ovcli.conf` therefore takes\neffect for the tools when DSH restarts the bundle, as it does for the runtime.\n\nTwo consequences follow from the proxy being one process per profile:\n\n- **MCP actor scope is process-level.** With the default `recallPeerScope: all`, MCP tool calls omit the actor peer header. With `actor`, they use the peer resolved at boot. Automatic recall, capture, and commit resolve their peer from each session's workspace.\n  Desktop boots the bundle in its profile directory, which is no repository, so\n  there the boot peer is empty and `actor`-scoped tool calls fall back to broad\n  recall. Set `actor_peer_id` in `ovcli.conf` or `OPENVIKING_PEER_ID` to give\n  them a peer; either one also overrides the workspace peer of every session.\n- **`remember` is not session-scoped.** The server's MCP `remember` stores into\n  its own short-lived session rather than the live `dsh-<session-id>` stream —\n  the same behavior the Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor integrations have.\n  Automatic capture still records the conversation itself.\n\nThe bridge and the skill provider are mounted last in `apply()`, after every\nlifecycle registration, so a proxy that cannot start holds up nothing above it.\n\n### Why the skill gets its own provider\n\n`skills.mjs` registers a second `ctx.skills` provider with\n`includeDefaultRoots: false` and `bundledSkillDir` pointing at `skills/`. DSH\nreads this host-owned bundle directly rather than asking a workspace filesystem\nto resolve a path outside its root. The provider discovers no project or user\nroots, so the bundle does not duplicate that catalog or override\nhigher-priority project skills. Those roots belong to DSH's own\n`skill-filesystem`: `dsh-base`'s host-level row in `headless`, `acp`, and\n`sdk`, whose app bundles keep it, and per-preset rows in `web` and `desktop`,\nwhere `dsh-web-app` disables the host row and the `standard`, `ptc`, and\n`cordis` agent presets each mount their own `skill-filesystem` and\n`tool-skill`. The bundle's provider registers at host level, which every\npreset reads, so those agents see the bundled skills. The `minimal` preset mounts no `tool-skill`, so its agents\nsee no skills, these included, and `sdk-minimal` has no `skills` service, so the\nprovider never starts there.\n\n## Configuration\n\nOpenViking credentials use the same resolution order as the other memory plugins:\n\n1. `OPENVIKING_*` environment variables\n2. `~/.openviking/ovcli.conf`\n3. `~/.openviking/ov.conf`\n\nCommon environment variables:\n\n| Variable | Purpose |\n| --- | --- |\n| `OPENVIKING_URL` / `OPENVIKING_BASE_URL` | OpenViking server endpoint |\n| `OPENVIKING_API_KEY` / `OPENVIKING_BEARER_TOKEN` | Bearer credential |\n| `OPENVIKING_ACCOUNT` | Trusted-mode account |\n| `OPENVIKING_USER` | Trusted-mode user |\n| `OPENVIKING_PEER_ID` | Explicit actor peer |\n| `OPENVIKING_WORKSPACE_PEER` | Derive a peer from each DSH session workspace's git identity by default; `0` sends no peer |\n| `OPENVIKING_RECALL_PEER_SCOPE` | `all` for cross-workspace recall or `actor` for isolation |\n\nThe profile's `cordis.patch.yml` can also carry plugin config:\n\n```yaml\n- id: openviking-memory-runtime\n  config:\n    endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:1933\n    recallMaxTokens: 2000\n    scoreThreshold: 0.35\n    captureToolResults: true\n    skipSubagentSessions: true\n    commitTokenThreshold: 20000\n    mcpToolCallTimeoutMs: 60000\n```\n\nRecall normally uses `POST /api/v1/search/search` with `mode: \"context\"`.\n`recallMaxTokens` (`OPENVIKING_RECALL_MAX_TOKENS`) sets this request's\n`max_tokens` budget for server-assembled context. When it is unset, the plugin\nomits `max_tokens` and uses the server's default budget.\n\n`recallLimit` (`OPENVIKING_RECALL_LIMIT`) scales the category quotas for context\nrecall; it is not a strict cap on the final number of entries. When explicitly\nset, it allocates at least one slot to each of the six categories: events,\nentities, preferences, experiences, resources, and skills. For example,\n`recallLimit: 4` sends six one-slot quotas, so the result can contain more than\nfour entries. Lowering it does not expand the set of categories searched.\nActual results still depend on matching content, score filtering, deduplication,\nand the token budget. When unset, the server's coding preset supplies the quotas.\n\nThe older size settings apply to fallback recall, not the primary context request:\n\n- `recallTokenBudget` (`OPENVIKING_RECALL_TOKEN_BUDGET`) controls the estimated\n  token budget of the locally rendered block when both server-side context and\n  the legacy `/api/v1/search/recall` endpoint are unavailable and recall falls\n  back to raw search results.\n- `recallMaxContentChars` (`OPENVIKING_RECALL_MAX_CONTENT_CHARS`) limits each\n  item's content in that local fallback. It also sets the legacy `/recall`\n  request's `max_chars` to `max(1000, recallMaxContentChars * recallLimit)`.\n\n## Behavior\n\n- Agent startup injects the OpenViking profile, the available-memory index, and the `<available-skills>` catalog through `agent.inject()`, and registers the per-session disposal commit. On DSH `0.1.7` and later this runs from the serial `agent/created` event (`{ agent, source, signal? }`), which holds queued input until it settles; DSH `0.1.0-rc.6` and `0.1.5` emit `agent/created` without `source` and start the session through `agent/session-start` instead. Startup runs once per agent, and `agent/pre-step` delivers the profile only if startup did not.\n- `agent/pre-step` retrieves with the current step input and appends a durable plugin message to that same step.\n- `session/event` captures user, assistant, and optionally tool-result messages without scraping a transcript.\n- `turn/end` checks the OpenViking pending-token threshold and commits when required.\n- `skipSubagentSessions: true` excludes sessions marked with `header.origin: subagent` from automatic profile, recall, capture, and commit; it defaults to `false`.\n- `syncTurns: false` stops every new write: no captured messages, no threshold or shutdown commit. Writes queued while the toggle was on are still replayed by the background drainer once the server recovers — they were captured with the toggle on. Profile injection and recall are unaffected; it defaults to `true`.\n- `skillCatalog` (default `true`) and `skillCatalogTokenBudget` (default `1200`; `0` also turns the catalog off) govern `<available-skills>`. The catalog comes from one `GET /api/v1/skills?node_limit=200` call: the user's own skills first, then those shared under `viking://agent/skills` minus any whose name the user also owns, each description cut to about 40 tokens. Its budget is separate from `profileTokenBudget`. When the descriptions do not fit, the catalog lists names only (with a `... +N more` tail if even the names do not all fit); when not even one name fits, it shrinks to a one-line count; with no skills, or a server without the endpoint, it is omitted.\n- Failed writes enter the shared OpenViking pending queue. A background drainer (default every 60s, `OPENVIKING_PENDING_DRAIN_INTERVAL_MS`) probes the server health and replays the queue in-process, so a transient write failure recovers without restarting dsh; it does not consume the session-start retry budget. Session-start replays keep consuming retries as before.\n- `tools/pre-execute` denies a DSH filesystem tool (`read`, `glob`, `grep`, `edit`, `write`, `str_replace_editor`) whose path argument is a `viking://` URI, pointing the model at the bridged `mcp__openviking__*` tools instead. A `write` or `edit` under a skill directory (`viking://~/skills/...`, `viking://user/<id>/skills/...`, `viking://agent/skills/...`) points at `mcp__openviking__add_skill` instead, which creates or replaces a whole skill from its `SKILL.md` text. A `grep` whose pattern is `viking://` text still runs.\n- `tools/post-execute` lets a `bash` command (`pwsh` on Windows, where DSH mounts it in place of `bash`) that carries a `viking://` URI run unchanged and attaches a notice for the model: use the bridged tools if it meant OpenViking content, or ignore the notice when the URI is intentional data such as an `ov` argument or an HTTP payload.\n\nEach DSH session maps to `dsh-<session-id>` in OpenViking. IDs that contain Windows-invalid path characters are normalized to a readable underscore form plus a stable hash, so two native IDs cannot collapse onto the same OpenViking session; already-portable IDs keep their existing mapping. Existing sessions whose native IDs require normalization start a new OpenViking session after this upgrade. Workspace-derived actor peers are resolved per session and sent on every session-specific request: the peer is the git identity of the session's workspace — the normalized `origin` URL (`git@github.com:volcengine/OpenViking.git` becomes `github.com-volcengine-openviking`), else the repository root path, that fallback keeping the older rule where every non-letter-or-digit character becomes `-`. With the default peer settings, no peer is sent outside a git repository, and what is remembered there goes to the user-level space `viking://user/<you>/memories`. One repository therefore keeps one peer across subdirectories, worktrees, clones and machines, while a fork's different origin keeps it separate. Memories written under the older path-derived peer stay reachable: the default `recallPeerScope: all` sweeps every peer under the user.\n\nWorkspace peer settings are loaded from `session.header.cwd` when the session first uses memory. A workspace can set `peer.id` to name its project explicitly, or `peer.source` to choose a preset or template chain. For example, `<root>/.openviking/config.json` can contain:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"version\": 1,\n  \"peer\": { \"id\": \"my-project\" }\n}\n```\n\nThe shared loader also applies `config.local.json` and machine registry overrides. Explicit host `peerId`, environment overrides and pinned `ovcli.conf` credentials retain their existing precedence. The resolved peer stays fixed for the session's runtime state; new sessions load the current workspace settings. A session without a cwd falls back to the process's working directory.\n\n## Tools\n\nThe model sees the OpenViking MCP tools under the bridge's server-qualified\nnames — `mcp__openviking__search`, `mcp__openviking__read`,\n`mcp__openviking__list`, `mcp__openviking__tree`, `mcp__openviking__grep`,\n`mcp__openviking__glob`, `mcp__openviking__remember`,\n`mcp__openviking__write`, `mcp__openviking__edit`,\n`mcp__openviking__forget`, `mcp__openviking__add_resource`,\n`mcp__openviking__add_skill`, `mcp__openviking__rule_search`, and the rest of\nwhatever the connected server\nadvertises. The list re-syncs when the server announces a change, so a server\nupgrade adds tools without a bundle release.\n\n`mcp__openviking__forget` performs permanent deletion. The calling model should\nuse it only when the user explicitly requests deletion.\n\nThe bundle also serves the shared `openviking-memory`, `openviking-skills`,\n`ov-experience-memory`, and `openviking-rule-search` skills from `skills/`\nthrough its own isolated `ctx.skills` provider, so the\nmodel gets the same guidance the other integrations ship: when to search, read,\nand write, and how to find, use, create, share, and migrate OpenViking skills.\n\n## Testing\n\n```bash\nnpm ci          # installs the exact-pinned dsh devDependencies the tests exercise\nnpm run check   # syntax check every shipped module + package/PLUGIN_VERSION agreement\nnpm test        # node --test *.test.mjs — runs in the repo's PR workflow\n```\n\nThe `0.3.2` compatibility check installed the packed bundle through\n`dsh plugin add` in isolated profiles and exercised DSH `0.1.0-rc.6`,\n`0.1.5-rc.1`, and `0.1.5-rc.2` with matching core packages. It covered Web startup\nand browser loading, skill discovery/read, MCP tool calls, profile/recall\ninjection, user/assistant capture, resume deduplication, threshold commits, and\ndisposal commits. The check used a local HTTP/MCP fixture and a deterministic\nmodel adapter on macOS with Node.js 26.5.0; it verifies harness integration, not\nreal-server memory extraction. The rc.2 CLI also exited cleanly on SIGTERM.\n\nThe startup failure from issue #4944 was reproduced by adding the reported\nold skill packages to an rc.2 profile; removing those direct dependencies and\nreinstalling the bundle restored the same integration checks. A clean rc.2\nprofile with the published `0.3.0` bundle did not reproduce that import error.\n\n`live-recall.test.mjs` is an opt-in end-to-end gate against a real OpenViking\nserver: it stores a sentinel memory through a session commit, waits for\nextraction, and asserts recall returns that sentinel — the property no stub\ncan certify. Enable it with `OPENVIKING_E2E=1` plus the normal credential\nchain; it skips otherwise (including in CI until a server secret exists).\n"

alt=\"volcengine%2FOpenViking | Trendshift\" style=\"width: 250px; height: 55px;\" width=\"250\" height=\"55\"/></a>\n\n</div>\n\n***\n\n## What is OpenViking\n\nOpenViking is an open-source context database for AI agents — one filesystem for everything an agent knows: knowledge, memory, and skills.\n\nMost agent memory is a black box: text goes in, embeddings come out, and nobody can see what was actually stored. OpenViking organizes context as a virtual filesystem under `viking://` instead. Agents navigate it like files — `ls`, `tree`, `read`, `write`, `grep` — and you can open any directory to inspect and edit what your agent knows. Every directory carries a generated summary, so agents can scan summaries first and decide what to read.\n\n<a href=\"https://studio.openviking.ai\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">\n  <picture>\n    <source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"docs/images/studio-filesystem-dark.png\">\n    <img src=\"docs/images/studio-filesystem.png\" alt=\"OpenViking Studio Filesystem: browse personal memories and resources\">\n  </picture>\n</a>\n\n[Try OpenViking Studio](https://studio.openviking.ai) in your browser, no installation required. [Self-host Web Studio](web-studio/README.md).\n\n## Why OpenViking\n\n- **One filesystem for knowledge, memory, and skills.** Resources hold documents and code; memories retain user preferences and experience; skills define how to perform tasks — not just extracted facts, but the full context, each with a `viking://` URI for browsing and retrieval. → [Viking URI](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/concepts/04-viking-uri) · [Context types](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/concepts/02-context-types)\n- **Search a directory, not the whole index.** Scope semantic search to a project or memory subtree instead of scanning a flat vector pool. `find` runs a query directly; `search` plans retrieval from session context. → [Retrieval](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/concepts/07-retrieval)\n- **Read the summary before the source.** Generated directory abstracts (L0) and overviews (L1) let agents judge relevance before opening full content (L2). → [Context layers](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/concepts/03-context-layers)\n- **Sessions become files you can read.** Committing a session archives the conversation and extracts memories as Markdown you can inspect, edit, and merge. With VikingBot enabled, `ov compile` organizes source material into a wiki, knowledge graph, or report. → [Sessions](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/concepts/08-session) · [Context compilation](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/context-compilation/01-overview)\n\n[Architecture](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/concepts/01-architecture) · [Design rationale](https://blog.openviking.ai/post/openviking-context-database/)\n\n```\nviking://\n├── resources/              # Resources: project docs, repos, web pages, etc.\n│   └── my_project/\n│       ├── docs/\n│       │   ├── api/\n│       │   └── tutorials/\n│       └── src/\n└── user/\n    └── {user_id}/\n        ├── memories/\n        │   └── preferences/\n        │       ├── writing_style\n        │       └── coding_habits\n        ├── resources/\n        │   └── private_project/\n        ├── skills/\n        │   ├── search_code\n        │   └── analyze_data\n        └── peers/\n            └── web-visitor-alice/\n```\n\nThe three loading tiers:\n\n- **L0 (Abstract)**: a one-sentence summary for quick relevance checks.\n- **L1 (Overview)**: core information and usage scenarios for planning.\n- **L2 (Details)**: the full original data, read only when needed.\n\nSemantically processed directories carry L0/L1 summaries, so agents can judge relevance before reading full files:\n\n```\nviking://resources/my_project/\n├── .abstract.md           # L0: quick relevance check\n├── .overview.md           # L1: structure and key points\n└── docs/\n    ├── .abstract.md\n    ├── .overview.md\n    └── api/\n        ├── auth.md         # L2: full content, loaded on demand\n        └── endpoints.md\n```\n\n## Proof it works\n\nOpenViking 0.3.22 has been evaluated on long-conversation user memory (LoCoMo) and multi-turn agent tasks (tau2-bench). Full results and setup details, including knowledge-base QA, are in the [benchmark report](https://blog.openviking.ai/post/openviking-benchmark-results/); reproduction scripts live in [./benchmark](./benchmark).\n\nTo run your own experiments, follow the [RAG and Memory evaluation guide](benchmark/README.md) for routine VikingBot memory evaluation, published LoCoMo reproduction, separate mem0 prompt comparisons, and RAG evaluation.\n\nThe memory evaluation used [Doubao 2.0 Pro](https://console.volcengine.com/ark/region:cn-beijing/model/detail?Id=doubao-seed-2-0-pro) as the VLM and [Doubao-embedding-vision-251215](https://console.volcengine.com/ark/region:cn-beijing/model/detail?Id=doubao-embedding-vision) as the embedding model.\n\n<picture>\n  <source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"docs/images/benchmark-dark.svg\">\n  <img alt=\"Benchmark results. LoCoMo accuracy: OpenClaw 24.20% native vs 82.08% with OpenViking; Hermes 33.38% vs 82.86%; Claude Code 57.21% vs 80.32%. tau2-bench task success: Retail 70.94% vs 77.81%; Airline 54.38% vs 66.25%.\" src=\"docs/images/benchmark-light.svg\">\n</picture>\n\n- **User memory (LoCoMo)**: with OpenViking, all three agent integrations land at 80–83% accuracy — up from 24–57% on their native memory — while input tokens drop by 34.3–91.0% and query latency by 58.45–66.10%.\n- **Agent experience (tau2-bench)**: experience memory lifts task success by +6.87pp (retail) and +11.87pp (airline) over the same LLM without memory.\n\n## Quick start\n\nSet up an OpenViking server first; if you already have one, skip to [Use it with your agent](#use-it-with-your-agent). Deploying your own needs uv, Python 3.10+ and a model provider with an embedding model and a VLM.\n\n<details open>\n<summary><strong>Let your agent deploy it</strong></summary>\n\n```text\nFollow this guide to install and start an OpenViking Server for me:\n\nhttps://docs.openviking.ai/en/getting-started/04-setup-for-agent\n\nAsk me for the model provider, the models, the workspace directory and whether\nother machines need to reach the server; don't guess. When you ask for the model\nAPI key, tell me how to hand it over if I'd rather not paste it into this chat,\nand never repeat it back.\n\nWhen it's running, tell me the server's address and whether auth is turned on.\n```\n\nYour agent will first ask which model provider to use and for its API key.\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Deploy it yourself</strong></summary>\n\nInstall OpenViking and run the setup wizard, which configures the models:\n\n```bash\nuv tool install openviking --upgrade && openviking-server init\n```\n\n`init` writes `~/.openviking/ov.conf` and supports Volcengine, OpenAI, Codex OAuth, Kimi, GLM and local Ollama; see the [configuration guide](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/guides/01-configuration). The server runs in the foreground, so keep this terminal open.\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Use OpenViking Service (hosted by Volcengine)</strong></summary>\n\nThe same OpenViking service, run for you by Volcengine. The first 50 files are free. Activate it on the [Volcengine product page](https://www.volcengine.com/product/openviking-service?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=readme), then create an API key in the console under User Management → API Key. The server address is `https://api.vikingdb.cn-beijing.volces.com/openviking`; you'll need it and the API key when you connect your agent.\n\n</details>\n\n### Explore with the CLI\n\nThe `openviking` package includes the `ov` CLI. With the server running, import a repository and search it:\n\n```bash\nov status\nov add-resource https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking\n# Replace TASK_ID with the returned task_id; repeat until status is completed\nov task status TASK_ID\nov ls viking://resources/\nov tree viking://resources/volcengine -L 2\nov find \"what is openviking\"\nov grep \"openviking\" --uri viking://resources/volcengine/OpenViking/docs/en\n```\n\n`ov find` returns matching context with URIs you can inspect. For client configuration (`ov config`), standalone CLI installs, and index maintenance, see [CLI setup](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/getting-started/05-cli-setup).\n\nBuild your own integration with the [Python](sdk/python/README.md), [Go](sdk/go/README.md), or [TypeScript](sdk/typescript/README.md) SDK, or the [HTTP API](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/api/01-overview).\n\n## Use it with your agent\n\nConnect your coding agent to OpenViking for cross-session memory. The memory plugin installer covers Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, TRAE, OpenCode and more, and detects which ones you have.\n\n<details open>\n<summary><strong>Let your agent install it</strong></summary>\n\n```text\nInstall the OpenViking memory plugin and help me start using it. OpenViking is a context database for AI agents (https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking); the command and link below are from its official docs.\n\n1. Run the official installer. It needs network access and writes to my home directory; if your sandbox blocks that, ask me for approval:\n   curl -fsSL https://openviking.ai/install | bash -s -- --yes --lang en --url <SERVER_URL> --api-key <API_KEY>\n2. Once it's installed, read the OpenViking onboarding guide and use it to walk me through setup. The guide has you ask me before choices like importing history or adding a working rule. docs.openviking.ai and docs.openviking.net are the same docs site; use whichever loads:\n   https://docs.openviking.ai/agents/en/onboarding.md\n\nThe API key is a user key I created for myself on that server; the installer stores it in ~/.openviking/ovcli.conf on this machine. Use it in the command as it is; there's no need to show it in your replies, and don't write it into any other file or rule. Talk to me in English.\n```\n\nBefore you send it, replace `<SERVER_URL>` with your server's address and `<API_KEY>` with a user key; a root key can't read or write memories. OpenViking open-sources a subset of these core capabilities.\n\n> **VikingMem: A Memory Base Management System for Stateful LLM-based Applications**<br>\n> Jiajie Fu, Junwen Chen, Mengzhao Wang, Aoxiang He, Maojia Sheng, Xiangyu Ke, Yifan Zhu, and Yunjun Gao.<br>\n> arXiv:2605.29640, 2026. Presented at VLDB 2026 in September.<br>\n> 📄 [Read the paper on arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29640) · [Read PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.29640)\n\n**Directory structure as retrieval context.** This paper provides the formal foundations, index design, and experimental evidence behind OpenViking’s directory-aware retrieval. It defines directory-scoped query and maintenance operations and introduces TrieHI, which OpenViking integrates to resolve directory scopes before vector ranking. This connects the filesystem paradigm to retrieval: agents can search a project or memory subtree, retain its surrounding context, and reorganize it as knowledge evolves.\n\n> **Directory-Aware Query and Maintenance in Vector Databases**<br>\n> Mengzhao Wang, Zheng Gong, Jingpei Hu, Jiajie Fu, Maojia Sheng, Junwen Chen, and Yifan Zhu.<br>\n> arXiv:2606.16903, 2026. Accepted by ICDE.<br>\n> 📄 [Read the paper on arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16903) · [Read PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.16903)\n\n**Retrieve the evidence you need with fewer tokens.** VikingRAG combines semantic search with document structure, exposing relevant directory segments as evidence gaps arise. Its core mechanisms are integrated into OpenViking. The paper further explores reusing retrieval traces and escalating to multi-round retrieval only when needed, reducing repeated exploration while preserving answer quality.\n\n> **VikingRAG: Accurate and Token-efficient Retrieval-augmented Generation over Structured Documents**<br>\n> Peiyuan Gao, Gaoyuan Zhang, Haojie Qin, Yahui Sun, Qianyi Zhang, Yunhao Zhang, Zeyu Wang, and Wei Lu.<br>\n> arXiv:2609.11390, 2026. Started here so every session shares one single-flight drainer.\n  runtime.startDrainer();\n  ctx.effect(\n    () => () => runtime.stopDrainer(),\n    \"openvikingMemory.stopDrainer()\",\n  );\n\n  // Per-agent startup: register the session's disposal commit, initialize the\n  // OpenViking session, and inject the profile while the agent is still idle.\n  // Runs at most once per agent, whichever DSH event reaches it.\n  const started = new WeakSet();\n  const startAgent = async (agent, signal) => {\n    if (skipMemory(agent.session) || started.has(agent)) return false;\n    started.add(agent);\n    agent.ctx.effect(\n      () => () => runtime.dispose(agent.session),\n      \"openvikingMemory.disposeSession()\",\n    );\n    try {\n      return await injectStartupProfile(agent, runtime, signal);\n    } catch (error) {\n      // A throw from a serial `agent/created` listener fails agent creation;\n      // memory startup must never do that. pre-step retries profile delivery.\n      runtime.log(\"startup_error\", {\n        error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),\n      });\n      return false;\n    }\n  };\n\n  // DSH 0.1.7+ has no `agent/session-start`; startup is the serial\n  // `agent/created` event with `{ agent, source, signal? }`, and AgentLoop holds\n  // queued input until its listeners settle. DSH 0.1.0-rc.6 and 0.1.5 still\n  // emit a composition-only `agent/created` with `{ agent }` only, followed by\n  // `agent/session-start`, so a missing `source` leaves startup to that event.\n  // The listener must resolve to undefined: any other value bails the serial\n  // dispatch and skips the listeners registered after this one.\n  ctx.on(\"agent/created\", async ({ agent, source, signal }) => {\n    if (source === undefined) return undefined;\n    await untilAborted(startAgent(agent, signal), signal);\n    return undefined;\n  });\n  ctx.on(\"agent/session-start\", ({ agent }) => startAgent(agent));\n\n  // prepend: downstream waterfall listeners run first, so this plugin sees\n  // the final claimed batch and appends after every other contributor.\n  // Profile + recall are independent after `next()`; run them concurrently so\n  // the agent/pre-step waterfall (which currently gates user/message push in\n  // dsh-agent-loop) spends less wall time (#4515).\n  ctx.on(\"agent/pre-step\", async ({ agent, messages, signal }, next) => {\n    const decision = await next();\n    if (skipMemory(agent.session)) return decision;\n    if (decision.kind !== \"enter\" || signal.aborted) return decision;\n    const [profile, recall] = await Promise.all([\n      runtime.profileMessage(agent),\n      runtime.recallMessage(agent, decision.messages),\n    ]);\n    if (signal.aborted) return decision;\n    const additions = [profile, recall].filter(Boolean);\n    // Keep the rest of the decision: goal-round-driver marks its entries with\n    // `startsRequestSeries`, and rebuilding the object would drop that flag.\n    return additions.length > 0\n      ? { ...decision, messages: [...decision.messages, ...additions] }\n      : decision;\n  }, { prepend: true });\n\n  ctx.on(\"session/event\", (session, event) => {\n    if (skipMemory(session)) return;\n    runtime.capture(session, event);\n    runtime.maybeCommit(session, event);\n  });\n\n  ctx.on(\"session/flush\", async session => {\n    if (skipMemory(session)) return;\n    await runtime.flush(session);\n  });\n\n  ctx.on(\"tools/pre-execute\", guardVikingUri);\n  ctx.on(\"tools/post-execute\", noticeVikingUri);\n\n  // Mounted last, and deliberately not awaited: the bridge's apply blocks on\n  // its first tools/list, so a server that accepts the connection but never\n  // answers would otherwise hold up every registration above it.\n  mountOpenVikingMcp(ctx, config);\n  mountOpenVikingSkills(ctx);\n}\n\n// Resolve when `promise` settles or `signal` aborts, whichever comes first. An\n// abandoned initialization keeps running and is reused by the pre-step path.\nfunction untilAborted(promise, signal) {\n  if (!signal) return promise;\n  if (signal.aborted) return Promise.resolve();\n  return new Promise(resolve => {\n    const onAbort = () => resolve();\n    signal.addEventListener(\"abort\", onAbort, { once: true });\n    promise.finally(() => {\n      signal.removeEventListener(\"abort\", onAbort);\n      resolve();\n    });\n  });\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * Every knob a memory plugin reads, declared once.\n *\n * A setting stayed uniform across harnesses only when a shared module read it\n * on the hot path: `recallLimit`, `scoreThreshold` and `captureMaxLength` agree\n * everywhere because `recall-core` and `capture-utils` read them.       "content": "/**\n * Local pending queue for offline resilience.\n *\n * When the OpenViking server is temporarily unreachable, write operations\n * (addMessage, commitSession) serialize their payloads to\n * `~/.openviking/pending/` as JSON files. If the\n * directory was created by a previous version of this code (or by hand)\n * with looser permissions, best-effort chmod it on first use.\n */\nasync function ensurePendingDir(dir) {\n  await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true, mode: PENDING_DIR_MODE });\n  try {\n    await chmod(dir, PENDING_DIR_MODE);\n  } catch {\n    // Best effort: chmod may fail on some platforms (e.g. Windows); not fatal.\n  }\n}\n\nfunction getPendingDir() {\n  return process.env.OPENVIKING_PENDING_DIR || DEFAULT_PENDING_DIR();\n}\n\nfunction getMaxRetries() {\n  const v = parseInt(process.env.OPENVIKING_PENDING_MAX_RETRIES || \"\", 10);\n  return Number.isFinite(v) && v >= 0 ? Avoids leaving a half-written JSON if the process\n  // crashes mid-write.\n  const tmpFilename = `${newFilename}.tmp.${process.pid}.${Date.now()}`;\n  try {\n    await writeFile(join(dir, tmpFilename), JSON.stringify(entry), {\n      encoding: \"utf-8\",\n      flag: \"wx\",\n      mode: PENDING_FILE_MODE,\n    });\n    await rename(join(dir, tmpFilename), join(dir, newFilename));\n    await unlink(join(dir, filename)).catch(() => {});\n    return true;\n  } catch {\n    await unlink(join(dir, tmpFilename)).catch(() => {});\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Clean up stale entries older than TTL.\n */\nexport async function cleanStale() {\n  const ttlMs = getTTLDays() * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;\n  const now = Date.now();\n  const pending = await listPending();\n  let cleaned = 0;\n\n  for (const { filename, entry } of pending) {\n    const age = now - (entry.createdAt || 0);\n    if (age > ttlMs) {\n      await dequeue(filename);\n      cleaned++;\n    }\n  }\n  return cleaned;\n}\n\n/**\n * Replay pending entries.
